channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Valdemar diz que Daniella Marques 'não tem voto' como vice de Flávio e sugere Tereza Cristina
item.description: PL national president Valdemar Costa Neto stated that economist Daniella Marques 'has no vote' as a vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 ticket, suggesting Tereza Cristina as a more electorally viable alternative.

item.title: Moraes lista 185 visitas recebidas por Bolsonaro em prisão domiciliar
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes cited that Jair Bolsonaro received 185 visits during his house arrest to justify a 30-day suspension of family visits and stricter restrictions. The decision maintains Bolsonaro under house arrest, reinforcing monitoring of the former president.

item.title: Eleitores de Lula se informam mais por rádio e TV; os de Flávio, pelas redes sociais
item.description: Lula's supporters are more likely to get news from radio and TV, where he leads with 51% and 52%, while Flávio Bolsonaro's base relies mainly on social media, where he has 35% versus Lula's 33%. Lula holds a narrow edge on websites and blogs (34% vs 31%) and leads among those who don't seek information (27% vs 17%). In a potential runoff, Lula wins among radio/TV users and the uninformed, but loses to all opponents among social media and online news consumers.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro promete celulares e internet de graça para mulheres
item.description: Senator and presidential pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro proposed distributing free smartphones and providing free internet access to women and the elderly as part of an inclusion plan aimed at reducing domestic violence and enabling access to government portals for reporting abuse and vocational training. Announced during a live stream with former Caixa head Daniella Marques, the initiative could reach up to 70 million women, prioritizing those who cannot afford devices. Bolsonaro said telecom companies have expressed interest, though providing basic smartphones to Bolsa Família beneficiaries alone would cost an estimated R$ 20.1 billion, excluding data plans.

item.title: Frase do dia
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated he had told U.S. President Donald Trump three times that Brazil has no interest in war and seeks peace. He said he now wants to wage a 'war of truth' to prove who is telling the truth in the tariff dispute between Brazil and the U.S. The remarks came amid rising trade tensions between the two nations.

item.title: Flávio chama decisão de Moraes sobre Bolsonaro de “ilegal” e “covarde”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) labeled the decision by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes as "illegal" and "cowardly", accusing the magistrate of political motivation for maintaining Jair Bolsonaro under house arrest and expanding restrictions. The pre-candidate for presidency made the statements in a video posted on social media.

item.title: STF vai acelerar debate sobre barreiras a pautas-bomba
item.description: The STF is set to accelerate discussions on barriers to 'budget-bomb' proposals, viewing the approval of the PEC for special retirement for community health agents as evidence that the Court will likely invalidate high-impact fiscal measures lacking fiscal responsibility compliance. In August, Minister Gilmar Mendes is expected to advance a binding súmula to solidify this stance. Additional topics include postponing the Code of Ethics debate until after elections, jurist Joaquim Falcão’s criticism of an alleged 'collusion' among powers, and the TSE’s push for an 'accuracy seal' on electoral polls to counter digital manipulation and opaque funding in low-cost surveys.

item.title: Filhos de Bolsonaro reagem à proibição de visita ao pai por 30 dias
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro's sons criticized a decision by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes to ban visits to the former president for 30 days after he violated restrictive measures. They called the ruling disproportionate, comparing it to Lula's treatment in prison and alleging a 'double standard'. Moraes clarified that Bolsonaro still receives visits from lawyers, doctors, and family members, including his wife and daughter, ensuring his legal defense remains fully accessible.

item.title: Como a ‘oligarquia parlamentar’ capturou as emendas
item.description: Over a decade, a 'parliamentary oligarchy' has captured the budget amendment process, allowing unelected politicians like Valdemar Costa Neto and Eduardo Cunha to influence public fund allocations. The system includes binding amendments that the executive cannot block and 'amendments Pix' that transfer funds with minimal oversight. The Supreme Federal Court is reviewing their constitutionality, with rulings expected in August on cases brought by PSOL and the Prosecutor General's Office.

item.title: Em 3 anos, diretor da PF ficou 81 dias em viagens com Lula
item.description: The director-general of the Federal Police, Andrei Rodrigues, accompanied President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on 19 of his 47 international trips during the third term, spending a total of 81 days across 20 countries. His presence exceeds that of many Esplanada ministers, indicating high institutional prestige, including participation in G7 summits and the first state visit to Washington under Donald Trump. The PF states that, besides presidential security, Andrei pursued an independent institutional agenda, signing international cooperation agreements during these missions.

item.title: Michelle estava em grupo de oração quando Bolsonaro deu carta a Flávio
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro was not informed in advance about the letter written by Jair Bolsonaro that designated Flávio Bolsonaro as a pre-candidate for the presidency in 2026, as she was in a prayer group during its drafting and only saw the content after the live broadcast. The former first lady expressed concern that the document's disclosure could increase the risk of new judicial rulings against the former president, especially following Justice Alexandre de Moraes’ extension of restrictions banning political-electoral visits until the end of the 2026 general elections.

item.title: Michelle muda esquema de segurança após ataques nas redes
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro's team has decided to strengthen her security scheme after identifying social media attacks since late June, when she posted a video criticizing her stepson, Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for president in 2026. The online hostility prompted a protocol change to ensure her safety.

item.title: Jaques Wagner tentou vender terreno de R$ 15 milhões um dia após ser alvo da PF, mas cartório barrou
item.description: Senator Jaques Wagner attempted to sell a plot of land for R$15.8 million one day after being targeted by the Federal Police in Operation Compliance Zero, but the property registry blocked the transfer following an order from Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça. Despite the block, he allegedly received at least R$12 million from the transactions, including the sale of his Salvador apartment for R$10 million. Wagner, who stepped down as Lula’s Senate leader after the operation, is a 2026 reelection candidate and denies wrongdoing through his legal team.

item.title: Da tornozeleira à prisão: Bolsonaro completa 1 ano com medidas restritivas, mas influência mexe com Eleições 2026
item.description: One year ago, on July 18, 2025, Jair Bolsonaro began wearing an electronic ankle monitor by order of Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, with restrictions including a ban on approaching embassies, using social media, and leaving home after 7 p.m. Since then, developments have included house arrest, conviction for attempted coup, transfer to the prison system, and internal PL conflict between Michelle and Flávio Bolsonaro over political support, with Bolsonaro ultimately backing his son’s presidential bid while Michelle maintained her Senate pre-candidacy.

item.title: Tarifaço: quais os riscos e ganhos se o Brasil adotar a reciprocidade? Entenda o que está em jogo
item.description: The Brazilian government is considering invoking the Economic Reciprocity Law in response to the 25% additional tariff imposed by the United States on products such as ethanol, agricultural machinery, and paper. Despite a firm political stance, experts note that activating the law requires a lengthy process involving public consultations and negotiations with the U.S., making an immediate response unlikely. The main risk highlighted is the potential increase in consumer prices if Brazilian retaliatory measures target American goods.

item.title: Lula prepara agenda de campanha e prevê ida a palanques prioritários
item.description: Lula da Silva will begin his 2026 re-election campaign with events in São Paulo starting July 20, including the convention formalizing Fernando Haddad's gubernatorial bid and, on August 2, his own presidential candidacy with Geraldo Alckmin as running mate. The campaign's inaugural act is set for August 16 in São Bernardo do Campo, a symbolic site in his political history.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro querem que Valdemar assuma as costuras políticas da campanha
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro are urging Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL party, to take charge of the political articulation for Jair Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential campaign. The push aims to strengthen internal party alignment and ensure strategic cohesion. This is an excerpt from a subscriber-only article.

item.title: Briga com Michelle deixa de ser ruído e pesa contra Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The public feud between Flávio Bolsonaro and Michelle Bolsonaro has moved beyond mere noise and is now affecting his pre-campaign, according to a Genial/Quaest poll: 42% of respondents side more with Michelle, while only 18% support Flávio. The dispute, sparked by disagreements over the PL’s slate in Ceará, was intensified by Michelle’s video, which 45% viewed as justified.

item.title: Lula amplia visitas ao Rio, afaga Ricardo Couto e busca reverter derrotas nos últimos 8 anos no estado
item.description: President Lula intensified his visits to Rio de Janeiro to regain political ground in the state, strengthening alliances with interim governor Ricardo Couto and former mayor Eduardo Paes. During a meeting at Fiocruz, Lula praised Couto, who became emotional recalling the Propag debt refinancing program, as the PT seeks to reverse eight years of electoral decline in the state following Bolsonaro's rise in 2018.

item.title: Bolsonaro recebeu 185 visitas desde o início da prisão domiciliar
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro received 185 visits since the start of his house arrest on March 27, according to Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. A visit by his son Flávio Bolsonaro, who read a letter written by Bolsonaro on social media, violated court orders, leading to a 30-day suspension of Bolsonaro's visitation rights (except for lawyers, doctors, and physiotherapists) and a 90-day ban on Flávio visiting him. Politically motivated visits remain prohibited until the end of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Filhos e aliados de Bolsonaro reagem à suspensão de visitas
item.description: Children and allies of Jair Bolsonaro reacted to Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision to keep the former president under house arrest but restrict visits to only doctors, physiotherapists, and lawyers for 30 days. Flávio, Carlos, and Jair Renan Bolsonaro condemned the measure as illegal and disproportionate, while Sóstenes Cavalcante and Marcel van Hattem denounced it as a human rights violation and electoral interference.

item.title: TARIFAÇO DO LULA, MORAES, FLÁVIO BOLSONARO E ELEIÇÕES 2026 | Dan Berg no Factual News 📱
item.description: The video discusses the possibility of a 'tariff war' political strategy involving Lula, Alexandre de Moraes, and Flávio Bolsonaro in the context of the 2026 elections, suggesting institutional or economic maneuvers with electoral impact. The content, aired by Factual News, references tensions between branches of power and political families, though without presenting concrete evidence. The narrative points to a scenario of heightened polarization and the use of legal or fiscal instruments as political weapons.

item.title: 'Mais uma decisão ilegal, desproporcional, covarde e cruel', diz Flávio após Moraes impedir visitas a Jair Bolsonaro por 30 dias
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro criticized Alexandre de Moraes' STF decision banning political-electoral visits to Jair Bolsonaro during house arrest until October 2026, calling it illegal, disproportionate, cowardly, and cruel. He accused Moraes of using state power to satisfy personal whims and of attempting to interfere in the 2026 elections, as he allegedly did in 2022.

item.title: Brasil é vítima de tarifa-sanção de Trump, não é covarde nem vai capitular, diz ministro da Indústria
item.description: Industry Minister Márcio Elias Rosa states that the U.S. tariffs on Brazil are a political sanction targeting the Lula government, not a legitimate commercial measure. He asserts Brazil is not cowardly and will not capitulate to U.S. pressure.

item.title: Moraes: Bolsonaro vive situação “mais benéfica” do que 705 mil presos
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes upheld Jair Bolsonaro's humanitarian house arrest, stating his situation is 'incomparably more beneficial' than that of the 705,872 people incarcerated in Brazil's prison system. Although he found Bolsonaro violated precautionary measures by allowing the dissemination of a political letter through Flávio Bolsonaro, Moraes chose only to suspend visits for 30 days (except for lawyers, doctors, and physiotherapists) and ban visits with political-electoral purposes until the elections.

item.title: Valdemar diz que Daniella Marques ‘não tem voto’ para ser vice de Flávio e sugere Tereza Cristina
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL, said Daniella Marques 'has no vote' to be Flávio Bolsonaro's running mate and suggested Tereza Cristina as the ideal candidate, despite her indicating she would not accept the role. Moraes' decision suspended Bolsonaro's political-electoral visits until the end of the 2026 elections, formally preventing him from participating in the vice-presidential choice. Daniella Marques, former Caixa president and cofounder of Grupo Pra Elas, joined Flávio in launching the 'Brasil Por Elas' package, advocating economic policies for women.

item.title: O recado de Alexandre de Moraes a Flávio Bolsonaro: ‘Patética a alegação’
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes dismissed Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's claim that visitation restrictions on Jair Bolsonaro render him 'incommunicable', calling the allegation 'pathetic'. Moraes noted that Bolsonaro has received 185 visits since March, including 64 from lawyers and 70 from doctors, and affirmed that his legal communication remains fully intact. The ruling also upheld the restrictions due to Bolsonaro's breach of precautionary measures, citing a letter read by Flávio on social media.

item.title: Eleitor responsabiliza mais Lula do que Bolsonaro por bets, mas tema não decide voto, diz pesquisa
item.description: A More in Common/Ipsos-Ipec poll released on July 17, 2026, found that Brazilians hold President Lula's government more responsible for the rise of online betting (bets) than Bolsonaro's administration. Nevertheless, the issue of bets does not significantly affect voters' electoral decisions.

item.title: Governador interino do Rio se emociona ao agradecer a Lula e ouve gritos de ‘fica’
item.description: Ricardo Couto, interim governor of Rio de Janeiro, became emotional alongside President Lula during a Fiocruz event, thanking federal support and emphasizing 'social sensitivity' as a guide for public management, particularly following the Propag agreement. He highlighted the Women's Health Caravan as a symbol of this sensitivity and yielded the microphone to Lula amid crowd chants of 'stay'.

item.title: A alegação ‘patética’ do advogado de Flávio Bolsonaro, segundo Moraes
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes dismissed as 'pathetic' the claim by Flávio Bolsonaro's lawyer that visitation restrictions on former President Jair Bolsonaro would lead to incommunicado detention. Moraes emphasized that Bolsonaro is under house arrest with daily contact with family, security agents, and a cook, and that his situation is vastly better than that of over 700,000 incarcerated individuals. The ruling suspends all visits for 30 days, bans the dissemination of political-electoral manifestos by any means, and prohibits political-electoral visits until the end of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Leia a íntegra da decisão que mantém a domiciliar de Bolsonaro
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes upheld Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest despite finding violations of its conditions, reinforcing measures to prevent further breaches and warning that new violations could lead to revocation and return to closed regime. He also limited visits to Bolsonaro for 30 days, preserving medical, physiotherapy and lawyer access, following a video by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro sharing a 'Letter to Brazilians' in which the former president asks for votes for his son and designates him as his 'spokesperson' in the presidential race.

item.title: Bolsonaro recebeu 185 visitas desde o começo da prisão domiciliar, diz Moraes
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the STF stated that Jair Bolsonaro has received 185 visits since the beginning of his house arrest on March 27, 2026. The visits include family members, personal doctors, physiotherapists, lawyers, and service providers, with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro acting as his father’s lawyer. Moraes dismissed claims of incommunicability, arguing the visits show Bolsonaro is not isolated, and imposed a 30-day suspension of visits and a ban on disseminating political-electoral manifests.

item.title: Leia a íntegra da decisão de Moraes que impôs novas restrições a Bolsonaro
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes maintained Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest but imposed new restrictions: all visits suspended for 30 days and a ban on disseminating 'political-electoral manifestos' by any means. Political-electoral visits are also prohibited until the end of the 2026 elections, and Flávio Bolsonaro, barred from visiting his father for 90 days, was identified as the ex-president's lawyer in the ruling.

item.title: Moraes proíbe visitas a Bolsonaro por 30 dias, incluindo a do presidente argentino Javier Milei
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes upheld Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest but banned all visits for 30 days, allowing only doctors, physiotherapists, and lawyers. The decision followed a defense request for a visit from Argentine President Javier Milei, scheduled for July 25, and was motivated by Bolsonaro's violation of social media restrictions through a letter disseminated by his son Flávio. Moraes ruled the visit would have political-electoral purposes, which is prohibited given Bolsonaro's suspended political rights due to a final criminal conviction.

item.title: Milei poderá visitar Bolsonaro?
item.description: The defense of Jair Bolsonaro has requested authorization from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to allow the former president to receive a visit from Argentine President Javier Milei at his residence, where he is serving house arrest. The proposed meeting would take place on July 25, the same date as an internal event of the Liberal Party (PL). The request is currently under judicial review.

item.title: Pedro marca o primeiro gol do Flamengo contra o Olimpia em Brasília
item.description: Pedro scored Flamengo's first goal in the friendly against Olimpia in Brasília, netting in the 28th minute of the first half after a right-flank play assisted by Lino. The goal equalized the match, which was organized by Metrópoles Sports. The event is part of a series of sporting events promoted by Grupo Metrópoles' sports division in 2026, including state and national championships.

item.title: Moraes aponta privilégio após manter domiciliar de Bolsonaro: 'situação mais benéfica que 705 mil presos'
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes maintained Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest but tightened restrictions after finding the former president violated precautionary measures by disseminating, through his son Flávio Bolsonaro, a politically electoral letter. Moraes stated Bolsonaro's situation is 'incomparably more beneficial' than that of Brazil's 705,872 incarcerated individuals, while insisting humanitarian benefits do not constitute illegal privilege. The ruling includes a 30-day suspension of social visits, a 90-day ban on visits from Flávio Bolsonaro, and a prohibition on politically motivated visits or dissemination of political manifestos until the end of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Moraes deixa Bolsonaro em domiciliar, mas proíbe visita com fins eleitorais
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes upheld Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest but barred him from receiving visits with political-electoral purposes until the end of the 2026 elections. The ruling aims to prevent Bolsonaro from using his restricted period to campaign or mobilize political support while under judicial supervision.

item.title: Moraes mantém prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro e proíbe visitas por 30 dias
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes upheld the house arrest of Jair Bolsonaro and banned all visits for 30 days, allowing only healthcare professionals and lawyers. The ruling also prohibits political-electoral meetings and the dissemination of political manifestos through any channel until the October elections conclude.

item.title: Moraes suspende visitas e impõe novas restrições a Bolsonaro
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended visit rights and imposed new restrictions on former President Jair Bolsonaro for 30 days after he disseminated a politically electoral letter supporting his son Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 presidential pre-candidacy. Despite the violation of precautionary measures, Moraes maintained Bolsonaro under house arrest, in line with the PGR's opinion that returning to closed regime would be disproportionate. The ruling reinforces judicial oversight over political activities of individuals convicted for attempting a coup d'état.

item.title: Moraes suspende todas as visitas a Bolsonaro por 30 dias
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes suspended all visits to Jair Bolsonaro for 30 days, except for medical care, physiotherapy, and lawyer contact, after Senator Flávio Bolsonaro shared a letter from his father urging votes for himself on social media, violating bans on third-party social media use. The decision responds to a PGR request to clarify communication restrictions on the former president, who is serving a 27-year-and-3-month sentence under house arrest and has had his political rights suspended. Moraes also banned visits with political-electoral purposes until the end of the 2026 elections and prohibited the dissemination of political-electoral manifestos through third parties.

item.title: Moraes mantém Bolsonaro em casa, mas limita visitas por 30 dias
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes maintained Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest but limited visits to only doctors, physiotherapists, and lawyers for 30 days, banning any political-electoral activity through third parties until the end of the 2026 elections. The decision follows an incident in which Senator Flávio Bolsonaro released a letter written by his father urging votes for himself, violating prior rulings that prohibit the former president from using social media or intermediaries for campaign purposes.

item.title: Moraes mantém prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro, mas barra visitas de familiares e amplia restrições
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes maintained Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest, banning visits from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for 90 days and prohibiting political contacts until the October elections, while also blocking the release of new manifestos.

item.title: Moraes mantém Bolsonaro em prisão domiciliar, mas proíbe visitas e manifestos políticos e eleitorais
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes ruled that Jair Bolsonaro remains under house arrest but banned visits and political-electoral manifestations, including through third parties, after finding a breach of precautionary measures via a letter disseminated by his son Flávio Bolsonaro. The decision blocks the planned visit by Argentine President Javier Milei and limits contact to cohabiting family members, doctors, and already-engaged lawyers.

item.title: Moraes mantém domiciliar de Bolsonaro, mas proíbe visitas ‘eleitorais’ e a divulgação de manifestos
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes maintained Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest but banned visits and the dissemination of political-electoral manifestos for 30 days, extending the visit ban until the end of the elections. The restrictions were imposed after Flávio Bolsonaro read a letter written by his father in a live stream, which was deemed a violation of the house arrest conditions.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro promete celular e internet grátis para tentar atrair o eleitorado feminino
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro proposed distributing free smartphones and internet plans to women as part of a PL strategy to overcome his disadvantage among female voters in the 2026 elections. The initiative aims to attract support through targeted technological benefits.

item.title: Moraes mantém prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro e suspende visitas com finalidade 'político-eleitoral' até fim das Eleições 2026
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes maintained Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest but suspended visits with political-electoral purposes until the end of the 2026 Elections, also banning general visits for 30 days (except medical, physiotherapeutic, and legal). He further prohibited the dissemination of political-electoral manifestos by Bolsonaro or third parties, citing repeated violations of the precautionary measure, particularly through the 'Letter to Brazilians' involving his son Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Moraes mantém Bolsonaro em domiciliar, mas veta visitas ‘político-eleitorais’
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes maintained Jair Bolsonaro's house arrest but banned visits for 30 days and prohibited any politically motivated visits until the end of the 2026 elections, including the dissemination of manifestos by third parties. The decision followed Flávio Bolsonaro's live reading of a letter from his father, which Moraes deemed a violation of the conditions of house arrest. Moraes warned that further breaches could result in the revocation of house arrest and a return to closed regime.

item.title: Moraes suspende visitas políticas a Bolsonaro até o fim das eleições
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes expanded restrictions on former President Jair Bolsonaro, banning political-electoral visits until the end of the 2026 elections and suspending all visits for 30 days except for medical personnel. He also prohibited Bolsonaro from disseminating political-electoral manifestos or messages, even through third parties, after a letter written by Bolsonaro was shared by his son, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, on social media.

item.title: Joaquim Barbosa desiste de disputar a Presidência pelo DC
item.description: Former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa informed the Christian Democracy (DC) party that he will not run for President of Brazil in the 2026 elections, stating that the conditions he had set for his candidacy were not met by the party. The DC had launched his pre-candidacy in May, but Barbosa decided to withdraw from the race.
